title: Reserved Capacity Orchestration Playbook (differential headroom & graceful fallback)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Customers with reserved pools experience either unexpected throttling during short spikes or excessive cost from overprovisioning. We need a coherent orchestration playbook for reserved capacity that codifies differential headroom, temporal throttles, emergency reclaim, and graceful tenant fallback to ensure predictable SLAs and cost efficiency. This PRD defines requirements, success metrics, rollout strategy, and acceptance criteria for the orchestration APIs, control plane rules, and console UX needed to operate these behaviors.
goals: Define a deterministic headroom allocation algorithm that assigns transient burst credit proportional to recent tenant activity and SLA tier
Expose an operator-friendly API + console controls for configuring headroom, temporal throttle windows, and emergency reclaim thresholds per reservation
Guarantee 99.95% P95 request success for P0 tenants under modeled 30s-2min spikes within defined burst budgets
Provide observability (per-tenant token-level cost delta, headroom consumption, reclaimed capacity events) and alerts for anomalous burst patterns
non_goals: Building a new long-term capacity market or auction system — we will not implement cross-tenant market bidding in this phase
Replacing Dedicated autoscaler entirely — autoscaling tuning continues in parallel but outside the core orchestration playbook
Changing core runtime kernels or model-compatibility decisions — performance optimizations handled by infra team separately
requirements: REQ-1: Headroom Allocator: service that computes per-reservation headroom score using weighted recent QPS, token variance, and SLA tier; returns a numeric headroom fraction (0.0-1.0)
REQ-2: Temporal Throttle Profiles: operator-configurable windowed throttle profiles (short: 30s, medium: 2m, long: 10m) that limit sustained burst rate while allowing short spikes
REQ-3: Emergency Reclaim: rule engine to mark candidate idle warm nodes for reclaim when cluster shortage crosses threshold; supports soft and hard reclaim behaviors
REQ-4: Fallback Routing: control plane that can reroute requests from constrained reservations to pre-defined fallback model variants or region pools with transparent auditing
REQ-5: Reservation Hint API: SDK endpoint for customers to submit expected surge hints (start_time, expected_qps, preferred_fallback) that influence prewarm decisions
REQ-6: Console Controls: new UI panels to visualize headroom, configure profiles, and simulate reclaim decisions before committing
REQ-7: Telemetry: emit events for headroom allocation, throttle triggers, reclaim events, and fallback invocations with tenant identifiers and request samples
REQ-8: Safe Defaults: for customers without explicit configs, provide conservative headroom and a recommended short-window throttle profile
REQ-9: Audit & Rollback: any operator change must be recorded and support a two-click rollback in console with diff view
REQ-10: SLA-backed Behavior: document and enforce contract that P0 reservations get prioritized reclaim avoidance for at least 60% of headroom budget
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Headroom Allocator returns deterministic results for a fixed input seed; unit tests cover edge cases (zero traffic, bursty traffic, new tenant) and integration tests validate across 5 synthetic tenant traces

AC-2: Temporal throttles apply within 500ms of policy update and enforce limits such that sustained QPS above configured window is rejected or queued according to policy; end-to-end tests show less than 1% false positives
AC-3: Emergency reclaim can be simulated in staging with no customer-facing errors; reclaimed nodes are claimed only after soft reclaim grace period unless overridden by operator

AC-4: Fallback routing triggers for configured tenants when headroom exhausted and routed requests are logged; routed requests maintain model-compatibility guarantees and metadata includes original reservation id
AC-5: Reservation Hint API accepted and surfaced in control plane; prewarm jobs triggered within configured horizon and visible in console timeline
AC-6: Console shows headroom consumption heatmap and allows operator to change throttle profiles with preview; changes require confirmation and appear in audit log
AC-7: Telemetry for orchestration emits to existing metrics pipeline; dashboards include a headroom burn rate view and alert if aggregate reclaimed capacity exceeds 10% in 5min
AC-8: Canary rollout: feature enabled for internal tenants, then 5 pilot customers; no more than 2% increase in service error rate observed during pilot
AC-9: Documentation: updated API reference, operator runbook, and customer-facing doc published before general rollout
AC-10: Performance: orchestration control plane adds <50ms median extra latency to request routing decision in the path
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): Implement headroom allocator and telemetry; enable for internal tenants only
Phase 1 (pilot): Add temporal throttles and reservation hint API; invite 5 pilot customers across tiers; monitor SLOs for 2 weeks
Phase 2 (soft public): Console controls enabled for self-serve customers; emergency reclaim can be triggered by operators; open recommended defaults
Phase 3 (GA): Full enablement, docs, training for support and sales; expose billing breakdown for reclaimed vs reserved usage
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly aggressive reclaim may surface errors to customers. Mitigation: adopt multi-stage reclaim (soft grace, sample-based confirmation, hard reclaim) and conservative defaults
Risk: Headroom algorithm becomes a source of unpredictability. Mitigation: deterministic seeding for allocator decisions, and visible simulation tools in console
Risk: Pilot customers may not opt in. Mitigation: pick internal partner teams and offer temporary credits and hands-on support
